High triglycerides in pregnancy: results, risks and treatment Understand normal pregnancy lipid changes, severe triglyceride results, pancreatitis risk and an individual plan for food, activity and specialist treatment. Nettle tea in pregnancy: benefits, uncertainty and safer decisions Understand nettle leaf versus root, pregnancy safety gaps, nutrient and allergy claims, medicine checks and what to do after drinking a nettle product. Ultrasound at 29 weeks: purpose, findings and follow-up Understand why a scan may be offered at 29 weeks, what growth, fluid, placenta, Doppler and wellbeing checks can show, and when to seek urgent care. Planks during pregnancy: adapting core exercise and returning after birth Learn how pregnancy changes plank exercises, when to reduce the load, what abdominal doming means, and how to plan a gradual return after birth. When a pregnancy may not continue: diagnosis, viability and care Understand uncertain scans, confirmed pregnancy loss, ectopic and molar pregnancy, very early birth and how care, future pregnancy and support differ. Sequential prenatal screening: two stages, results and choices Understand linked first- and second-trimester screening, stepwise and contingent pathways, result limits and options after a higher-chance result. White mulberries in pregnancy: fresh fruit, dried fruit and safety Understand white mulberry nutrition, fresh versus dried fruit, allergy and blood-sugar claims, herbal products and what cravings can tell you. Induction of labour: benefits, risks and newborn care Understand why induction is offered, how timing and methods affect risks, what evidence says about cesarean birth, and when a newborn needs help. Dry eyes in pregnancy: symptoms, safe care and when to seek help Understand pregnancy-related dry-eye discomfort, contact lenses, lubricant choices, practical care and eye or maternity symptoms needing prompt assessment. Blurred vision in pregnancy: eye changes and when to get help Understand pregnancy-related focusing changes, dry eyes, glasses and contact lenses, with clear advice on urgent vision symptoms and follow-up after birth. Sunburn during pregnancy: care, medicines and prevention Soothe sunburn, check pain relief and skin products, recognise heat illness and plan sun protection during pregnancy without relying on tanning myths. Melatonin in pregnancy: safety, alternatives and better sleep Understand the limits of melatonin pregnancy evidence, how sleep medicines are assessed, and practical ways to address insomnia and its causes. Squats during pregnancy: choosing a comfortable, supported movement How to adapt pregnancy squats with a stable support, comfortable stance and depth, suitable loading, pelvic-pain advice and clear signs to stop. Pain medicines in pregnancy: paracetamol, NSAIDs, aspirin and opioids Compare pregnancy pain-relief options, timing-related risks, preventive aspirin and prescribed opioids, and know when pain or a medicine exposure needs care. Ultrasound at 13 weeks: timing, findings and next steps What an ultrasound around 13 weeks can show, how NT and screening windows vary, how to prepare, and what uncertain or unexpected findings mean. Too-frequent contractions in labour: tachysystole and monitoring Understand excessive contraction frequency, prolonged tightening, possible causes, fetal monitoring and clinical care: and when to call your maternity team urgently. High cholesterol in pregnancy: tests, FH and medicine decisions How to interpret rising cholesterol in pregnancy, plan treatment for familial hypercholesterolemia, and arrange safe medicine, feeding and postpartum follow-up. Unexpected pregnancy symptoms: nosebleeds, discharge, sleep and digestion Five pregnancy changes that may surprise you, practical comfort measures, and how to distinguish everyday symptoms from problems needing care. Can your eyes predict your baby’s sex? Why pupil changes and Y-shaped eye-vessel rules cannot give a dependable fetal-sex prediction, what both-eye claims mean, and what clinical tests can tell you. A sudden fright during pregnancy: reassurance, noise and when to get help Understand the startle response, worries about pregnancy loss, loud-noise exposure, calming steps and symptoms that need maternity or emergency assessment. Elderberry in pregnancy: evidence, preparation and safety What elderberry studies do and do not show, why cooked or commercial products do not prove pregnancy safety, and what to do after an exposure or with flu symptoms. Metformin before and during pregnancy: benefits, uncertainties and breastfeeding Why metformin may be prescribed for diabetes or PCOS, how pregnancy changes the decision, what fetal safety evidence shows and how to plan breastfeeding. Beetroot in pregnancy: benefits, limits and safe preparation How beetroot fits a pregnancy diet, what nitrate studies actually found, and how to handle folate, anaemia, red urine, diabetes, stones and preparation. Hibiscus tea in pregnancy and breastfeeding: what the evidence can tell you Understand roselle tea, animal studies, labour-induction claims, mixed herbal products and breastfeeding, plus what to do after an exposure or concerning symptoms. Kombucha in pregnancy and breastfeeding: safety and alternatives What fermented tea contains, why kombucha is best avoided in pregnancy, and how alcohol, caffeine, processing and feeding decisions differ during breastfeeding. Throat mucus in pregnancy: causes, relief and when to get help Distinguish nasal drainage from chest phlegm, consider reflux, allergy and asthma, and choose pregnancy-compatible care with clear warning signs. Gas and air in labour: nitrous oxide, pain relief and safety Understand nitrous oxide and oxygen in labour: self-held masks, timing, realistic pain relief, switching options, side effects, suitability and breastfeeding. Rheumatoid arthritis and birth: planning your delivery How rheumatoid arthritis can affect birth positions, pain relief, medicines and recovery, and why a caesarean is not automatically needed. Sneezing in pregnancy: causes, pain and safe relief What repeated sneezing means in pregnancy, how to ease nasal symptoms, and when abdominal pain, fever or breathing problems need care. Rhubarb in pregnancy: stalks, leaves and realistic benefits Separate culinary rhubarb stalks from poisonous leaves and medicinal roots, with nutrition, calcium, kidney, medicine and pregnancy safety limits. Ovarian torsion during pregnancy: symptoms, scans and urgent treatment Understand ovarian torsion in pregnancy, why normal blood flow does not exclude it, and how urgent surgery and early hormone support are considered. Green plums in pregnancy: benefits, sourness, salt and safety A practical look at green-plum nutrition, pregnancy benefit claims, reflux, teeth, salted fruit and individual kidney-stone advice. Methergine and retained pregnancy tissue: what treatment can and cannot do How retained pregnancy tissue is assessed, where methylergonovine may fit in bleeding care, and its contraindications, interactions and breastfeeding precautions. Ovarian cysts and rupture in pregnancy: types, assessment and care Understand cyst types and early pregnancy hormones, what rupture can mean, and how clinicians choose monitoring, pain relief or urgent treatment. Pubic-joint pain in pregnancy: assessment, support and recovery Understand pain at the pubic joint, how pelvic girdle pain differs from separation, useful support, imaging choices and when to seek urgent care. Leg cramps in pregnancy: relief, prevention and warning signs Recognise a calf cramp, try gentle relief and a supported stretch, understand mineral-supplement limits, and know when leg pain needs urgent care. Grapefruit in pregnancy: nutrition, juice and medicine safety Understand grapefruit nutrients and pregnancy benefit claims, choose and prepare fruit or juice safely, and check portions, medicines and seed extracts. Appendicitis in pregnancy: symptoms, scans, surgery and recovery How appendicitis can present in pregnancy, when pain needs urgent help, how scans and surgery are chosen, and what to expect during recovery. A baby born at 24 weeks: survival, neonatal care and development Understand individual survival estimates at 24 weeks, intensive care for warmth and breathing, eye and hearing checks, and longer-term developmental support. How early can a baby survive? Weeks, care and long-term outlook How gestational age, neonatal care and individual health affect survival after early birth, what study percentages mean, and which questions to ask your team. Tingling and numbness in pregnancy: hands, back, legs and when to get help Understand different patterns of pregnancy tingling, carpal tunnel, sciatica and outer-thigh numbness, practical care and symptoms that need urgent assessment. How accurate is ultrasound for detecting fetal conditions? Understand what a normal or concerning pregnancy ultrasound means, why detection rates vary, and how specialist scans and selected tests can clarify a finding. Isotretinoin and pregnancy: exposure, prevention and acne-care choices What to do after pregnancy or a contraceptive failure during isotretinoin treatment, why exposure matters, how waiting and local prevention programmes work, and options for acne care. Iron-deficiency anaemia before, during and after pregnancy How iron deficiency is assessed before conception, during pregnancy and after birth, with food, oral and IV treatment, follow-up, feeding support and urgent warning signs. Umbilical-cord cysts: scan findings, follow-up and your baby’s outlook Understand true cysts and pseudocysts, early resolving versus persistent findings, genetic-test choices, growth checks and individual birth planning. Fetal hydrops: causes, assessment, treatment and newborn care What immune and nonimmune fetal hydrops mean, how specialists investigate the cause, which treatments may help, and how maternal safety, birth and newborn care are planned. X-rays during pregnancy: dose, timing and decisions Understand necessary or unexpected X-ray exposure in pregnancy, fetal dose, timing, CT and dental imaging, shielding, and when to request an individual assessment. When to tell people you are pregnant: timing, privacy and support Decide when and whom to tell about pregnancy, balance early support with privacy, set sharing boundaries and keep care separate from a public announcement. Viral hepatitis in pregnancy: pregnancy loss, treatment and protecting the baby Compare hepatitis A–E in pregnancy, understand why risk depends on the virus and liver illness, and plan testing, treatment and newborn protection without relying on a fixed risk percentage. Zinc oxide in pregnancy: creams, sunscreen and other exposures Understand zinc oxide skin products in pregnancy and breastfeeding, how to follow their labels, and why oral zinc and workplace fumes need separate advice.

title: Newborn Care
description: The first months: feeding, sleep, daily care, and knowing when to call your doctor, plus recovery for you.
body: Newborn Care Basics: Your First Days at Home A calm, practical guide to your first days home with a newborn: feeding cues, sleep basics, safe handling, visitors, and learning to trust yourself as a parent. Breastfeeding: A Beginner’s Guide Getting started with breastfeeding: latch basics, how often newborns feed, common early challenges, signs baby is getting enough, and where to find real support. Formula Feeding: How to Bottle-Feed Safely A judgment-free guide to formula feeding: choosing a formula with your provider, safe preparation and sterilizing, amounts by age, and paced bottle feeding. Newborn Sleep: What’s Normal in the First Months What newborn sleep really looks like: total hours, short cycles, day–night confusion, safe sleep rules, gentle routines, and survival tips for exhausted parents. Bathing and Diapering Your Newborn How to bathe and diaper a newborn with confidence: sponge baths before the cord falls off, bath temperature and safety, diapering step-by-step, and preventing rash. Umbilical Cord Care and Common Newborn Skin Issues Simple umbilical cord care, signs of infection to watch for, and a reassuring guide to normal newborn skin: peeling, baby acne, cradle cap, and milia. Recognizing Illness in a Newborn: When to Call the Doctor A calm guide to newborn warning signs (fever, feeding refusal, breathing trouble, jaundice, dehydration, and lethargy) and why calling early is always right. Postpartum Recovery: Caring for Yourself After Birth What postpartum recovery really involves: healing after vaginal or cesarean birth, bleeding expectations, rest and nutrition, emotional shifts, and your own checkups. Soothing a Crying Baby and Understanding Colic Why babies cry, calming techniques that actually help, what colic is and is not, how to cope when nothing works, and when crying deserves a call to the doctor. Newborn Development: The First Three Months How newborns develop from birth to three months: reflexes, senses, tummy time, first social smiles, and easy everyday ways to support your baby’s growth. The First 24 Hours With a Newborn: What to Expect A calm, hour by hour guide to the first 24 hours with a newborn: the golden hour, the first feed, routine hospital care, diapers, sleep, and the wakeful second night. Newborn Hunger Cues: Early, Active, and Late Signs Learn to spot newborn hunger cues in three stages, from rooting and hands to mouth to crying, plus fullness signs and when to wake a sleepy baby for a feed. How to Get a Good Latch: Step by Step for Newborns Learn how to get a good latch step by step: positioning, the wide gape, chin-first attachment, signs of a good latch, and how to fix a shallow, painful latch. Breast Milk Storage Guidelines: Room, Fridge, Freezer Clear breast milk storage guidelines in one place: how long milk keeps at room temperature, in the fridge, and in the freezer, plus safe thawing, warming, and practical pumping basics. How to Prepare Baby Formula Safely: Water and Mixing Learn how to prepare baby formula safely: what water to use, exact mixing ratios, how long formula keeps after mixing, and simple bottle cleaning and sterilizing routines. How Many Wet Diapers Should a Newborn Have Each Day How many wet diapers should a newborn have? A day by day counting guide from birth through the first weeks, plus what brick dust means and the dehydration signs that need a call. Newborn Poop Colors: What Is Normal and What Is Not A calm newborn poop color guide: the normal timeline from meconium to yellow or tan stools, how often babies go, and which colors need a same-day call to your clinician. Newborn Jaundice: Causes, Timeline, and Treatment What newborn jaundice is, when it usually appears and fades, how bilirubin is checked, how feeding and phototherapy help, and the warning signs that need a prompt call. Newborn Fever: Why 100.4 F Means Call Right Away A rectal temperature of 100.4 F (38.0 C) or higher is a newborn fever that needs same day medical care. What to do, how to measure, and what to avoid. Safe Sleep for Newborns: The ABCs and Room Sharing Safe sleep for newborns comes down to the ABCs and room sharing: baby alone, on their back, in a bare crib, in your room for at least six months. How to Swaddle a Baby Safely and When to Stop A calm, step by step guide to how to swaddle a baby safely: the right tightness, hip healthy wrapping, night sleep rules, and when to stop swaddling. Normal Newborn Crying and the Period of PURPLE Crying The Period of PURPLE Crying describes the normal rise in newborn crying that peaks around 6 to 8 weeks. Learn how much crying is normal, what colic is, and how to cope. When to Introduce a Pacifier and How to Use It Safely When to introduce a pacifier, how it relates to safer sleep, cleaning and replacement basics, and a calm plan for taking it away later, based on mainstream guidance. Newborn Rash Guide: What Is Normal and When to Worry Most newborn rash types, including erythema toxicum, milia, baby acne, and peeling skin, are harmless and clear on their own. Here is how to recognize each one and when to call a clinician. How to Cut Newborn Nails Safely: Tools and Timing A calm, step by step guide to how to cut newborn nails: when to file instead of clip, how often to trim, and what to do if you nick the skin. Newborn First Doctor Visit: Timing and What to Expect When the newborn first doctor visit happens, what the checkup includes, what to bring, and the questions worth asking, laid out for tired parents heading to the first appointment. When to Start Tummy Time and How Long Each Day When to start tummy time, how long each newborn session should be, and how many times a day to aim for, plus positions for babies who protest. How to Sleep When You Have a Newborn: A Rest Plan A practical guide to how to sleep when you have a newborn: night shifts, one protected anchor block, short naps, caffeine timing, and the safety rules every exhausted parent needs. Cluster Feeding and Rest: A Plan for the Early Weeks How to understand frequent newborn feeding periods, protect parent rest, share practical work, and recognize when feeding concerns need professional support. Paced Bottle Feeding: A Calm, Responsive Technique How paced bottle feeding works, how to notice a newborn’s cues, choose a comfortable position, reduce pressure to finish, and know when feeding support is needed. Babywearing Safety: A Simple Fit and Airway Check How to choose and adjust a newborn carrier, keep the baby’s airway visible, move safely, and know when to ask for a fit check. Newborn Temperature and Dressing: Simple Layers, Safer Sleep How to judge a newborn’s comfort, choose breathable layers, avoid overheating, check the room, and respond to signs of illness. Postpartum Bleeding: What Recovery Can Look Like and When to Call A non-graphic guide to normal postpartum bleeding changes, rest and hygiene, warning signs, and how to prepare for a timely call to your care team. Postpartum Mood Changes: Support for the Parent, Too How to tell the difference between common early emotional changes and symptoms that deserve professional support, with practical ways partners can help. Umbilical Cord Healing: Gentle Care and What to Watch How to keep a newborn’s umbilical cord clean and dry, protect it from rubbing, recognize expected changes, and identify signs of infection. Baby Growth Spurts: When They Happen and What to Expect When baby growth spurts usually happen, the signs to expect, how long they last, and how to tell a normal hungry stretch from something that needs a clinician. Vaginal dryness after birth: causes, comfort and treatment Understand postpartum hormones, breastfeeding, thyroid symptoms and the difference between everyday comfort measures and prescribed treatment. Hair shedding after birth and caring for your hair Understand postpartum hormonal shedding, the usual timetable, four practical care options and when to check for another cause. Constipation while breastfeeding: relief, laxatives and a safer care plan Understand postpartum constipation, each main laxative type, breastfeeding considerations, medicine interactions and the symptoms that need prompt assessment. When your baby is not gaining weight as expected Understanding early weight loss, feeding difficulties and other causes of slow gain, with practical steps for a safe, individualized feeding review. A breast lump during breastfeeding: getting it checked Understand mastitis, abscesses, fibroadenomas and galactoceles, breast-cancer warning signs, and how tests or treatment affect breastfeeding. Home phototherapy for newborn jaundice: equipment, care and follow-up How supervised home phototherapy works, how the devices differ, and what parents need to know about setup, feeding, monitoring and getting help. Recognising newborn jaundice and understanding bilirubin tests Learn what yellow skin can and cannot show, how skin and blood bilirubin tests differ and which newborn symptoms need urgent assessment. Breastfeeding and newborn jaundice: keeping feeding and treatment together Why newborn jaundice happens, how feeding affects bilirubin, warning signs, and what to expect from tests, phototherapy and follow-up. After the umbilical cord falls off: caring for the healing navel Know how to care for the healing belly button, what a little blood can mean, and which skin or newborn illness signs need prompt help. A slim baby or a growth concern? How to tell the difference How growth charts, feeding, birth history and health help distinguish a naturally small baby from one who needs growth support. Breastfeeding and sexual wellbeing after birth How feeding, hormones, healing and daily life can affect desire and comfort, with practical help for leakage, communication and contraception. Should you feed your baby after they vomit? Learn when to offer another milk feed, how to manage small amounts and which vomiting or dehydration signs need urgent care. Choosing contraception while breastfeeding Compare breastfeeding-compatible contraception, understand when breastfeeding itself can help prevent pregnancy, and plan for missed pills or unprotected sex. Fever after birth: when to get medical help Causes of postpartum fever, symptoms to report, treatment and practical recovery care. A temperature of 38°C or higher needs prompt assessment. Why babies rub their eyes Understand tiredness, irritation and other reasons for eye rubbing, with gentle care and clear signs that need an eye assessment. Fertility and pregnancy spacing after birth Pregnancy can happen before periods return, including during breastfeeding. Planning the next pregnancy involves recovery, contraception and your individual circumstances. Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis after birth: symptoms, tests and treatment Understand this uncommon infected pelvic-vein clot, why persistent postpartum fever needs assessment, and how antibiotics, scans and blood thinners are used. Why a baby may bring up formula after a feed Understand the difference between spit-up and vomiting, possible feeding and medical causes, and which changes need prompt assessment. Galactosemia: understanding the diagnosis and feeding plan Learn how galactosemia types differ, why newborn follow-up is urgent, and how specialist feeding, nutrition and developmental care support a child. Combining breastfeeding and pumping: a comfortable, practical plan Fit expressing around direct feeds, use a pump comfortably, understand power pumping and handle milk safely without creating unnecessary oversupply. Gentle routines for newborn sleep Build a flexible newborn routine around feeding, safe sleep, brief play and support for tired caregivers. Baby babbling: sounds, stages and first conversations Understand cooing, repeated syllables and early conversation, with everyday ways to respond and signs that deserve a hearing or developmental check. Is my milk supply really low? Signs, causes and a practical feeding plan Understand newborn diapers and weight, normal breastfeeding changes, possible supply problems and when to get help before trying pumps, teas or supplements. Pelvic-floor recovery after birth: eight things worth knowing Understand leakage, pelvic pain, muscle tension, sex and postpartum pelvic-health appointments, with practical guidance on exercise and when to seek help. When your baby is not feeding well Recognise urgent feeding changes, understand common and less common causes, and build a plan for milk intake, early solids and follow-up. Can a baby have too much milk? Use feeding cues and growth checks to guide milk feeds without pressuring a baby or judging their body shape. Mucus in your baby’s stool: look at the whole picture A slimy-looking stool is not a diagnosis. Feeding, hydration, fever, blood, vomiting and your baby’s behaviour help determine the next step. Blood clots and bleeding after birth: when to get help A practical guide to lochia, changes during the first six weeks, vaginal clots, urgent warning signs and assessment of abnormal bleeding after birth. A chalazion while breastfeeding: caring for an eyelid lump How a chalazion differs from a stye, gentle home care, breastfeeding treatment questions and when an eyelid lump needs assessment. Reflux in babies: common signs and symptoms that need help Spitting up is often normal, but poor feeding, poor growth and unusual vomiting need assessment. Crying or back arching alone does not diagnose reflux disease. When your baby does not want a pacifier Gentle ways to offer a pacifier, feeding and sleep safety, which tricks to avoid, and how to comfort a baby who simply does not want one. Recovering after a cesarean birth A practical guide to rest, movement, incision care and asking for support while recovering from a cesarean. Is your baby overheating? Signs, cooling and prevention Recognise when a baby is too hot, keep feeding and sleep safe in every season, and know which changes need urgent medical help. Diarrhea after birth: causes and getting help Understand loose stools after vaginal or cesarean birth, including antibiotic effects, bowel-control problems, hydration and treatment while breastfeeding. Vaginal bleeding after a cesarean What lochia can look like after a cesarean, how to manage pads and wound care, and which bleeding changes need urgent medical attention. Understanding a retained placenta Why a placenta may not deliver after birth, how timing and symptoms guide care, and what to expect from removal, recovery and future birth planning. When pumping hurts your nipples: finding the cause and relief Check flange fit, suction and existing nipple damage, understand engorgement and infection, and learn when painful pumping needs professional help. Flu vaccination for babies: age, protection and what to expect Understand when babies can receive flu vaccine, how to protect younger infants, dose schedules, common reactions and symptoms needing urgent help. Expressing milk at work: planning your day and storing milk safely Plan breaks, pump fit, cleaning, milk storage and the journey home so expressing at work becomes manageable without rigid targets or unnecessary purchases. Why babies smile or laugh in their sleep Normal active sleep, the limits of interpreting a baby’s dreams, and the repeated or unusual events that need medical assessment. When do babies start to laugh? Smiles, chuckles and fuller laughs develop gradually. Try gentle shared play and know when to discuss a missed milestone with your baby’s clinician. Why newborns startle in their sleep Understand the Moro reflex, safe ways to settle a baby and when unusual jerking needs medical assessment. Trying laid-back breastfeeding Learn how a supported recline can help you explore comfortable feeding, with practical positioning, caesarean adaptations and clear sleep-safety boundaries. When your baby suddenly refuses the breast A nursing strike can be temporary, but keeping a baby fed and recognising illness come first. Get practical support without forcing a feed. Could a baby have haemorrhoids? Haemorrhoids are unusual in babies. Blood in the nappy or a lump around the anus needs assessment for more common causes and appropriate treatment. Cupping while breastfeeding: evidence and risks Understand dry and wet cupping, the limits of claimed benefits, and why blood loss, skin injury and postpartum symptoms need individual assessment. Leech therapy and breastfeeding: distinguish surgical care from wellness claims Medicinal leeches have a specific monitored use in reconstructive surgery; that does not validate broad claims about health or breastfeeding. Using acetaminophen for teething pain: comfort, dosing checks and warning signs When a pain reliever may help sore gums, how to check the exact medicine, and when unsettled behaviour needs more than a teething explanation. Helping a teething baby settle at night Nine practical ways to support a teething baby, with safe cooling, medicine precautions, sleep guidance and signs that need medical attention. Returning to sex after a cesarean birth Recovery, comfort and readiness all matter after a cesarean. Find practical ways to reconnect, manage dryness and get help when sex hurts. Could a painful cesarean-scar lump be endometriosis? Scar endometriosis is an uncommon cause of a painful lump after cesarean birth. Learn the clues, other possibilities and how clinicians assess and treat it. Vitamin C for babies: food, milk and supplements Babies need vitamin C, but an intake target is not a supplement dose. Learn how feeding and local vitamin guidance fit together. Hernia after pregnancy: symptoms, treatment and recovery Recognize a possible postpartum hernia, distinguish it from abdominal muscle separation, and understand monitoring, surgery and future pregnancy planning. A hernia near a cesarean scar: symptoms, assessment and repair Learn how an incisional hernia can appear after a cesarean, which symptoms need urgent care, how diagnosis works and what to discuss about repair and future pregnancy. Rest after birth: recovery without prolonged bed rest Recovery needs rest and practical support, but staying in bed all day is not a routine way to prevent complications. Build a plan around your birth and symptoms. Blue or grey lips in a baby: when to get help Blue-baby syndrome describes a warning sign, not one diagnosis. Learn why colour changes need prompt assessment and how safe water helps prevent one cause. Can you eat spicy foods while breastfeeding? Understand spicy meals, flavour changes in milk, the garlic research, infant symptoms and the food restrictions that deserve individual advice. Vitamin A while breastfeeding: food, supplements and skin products How vitamin A supports you and your baby, what recommended amounts mean, and why high-dose supplements and retinoid skin treatments need separate advice. Why does my baby wake crying or screaming? Nine possible reasons for distressed night waking, how to check feeding and comfort, and when illness or caregiver exhaustion needs help. The sucking reflex and your baby’s feeding skills How sucking and rooting support feeding, why premature babies may need help, and what other newborn reflexes can tell the care team. Why does my baby shake or turn their head? Some head movements are part of feeding, play or settling. Sudden clusters, altered awareness or developmental changes need prompt assessment. Back sleeping, side sleeping and a baby who rolls Why babies should start every sleep on their backs, what changes with independent rolling, and how to handle reflux, flat spots, swaddling and other concerns. Necrotising enterocolitis: signs, treatment and recovery NEC is a serious intestinal illness in newborns. Learn which changes need urgent attention and how neonatal teams investigate and treat it. Preventing abusive head trauma: safe care when a baby cries Recognise possible abusive head trauma, know when to call emergency services and make a practical plan to keep a baby safe when caregivers feel overwhelmed. Choanal atresia: blocked nasal passages in babies and children Learn how one-sided and two-sided choanal atresia differ, which breathing signs are urgent, and how diagnosis, surgery and follow-up work. FPIES: recognising a delayed food-allergy reaction Learn the delayed and chronic patterns of FPIES, emergency signs, diagnosis, feeding choices and how tolerance is assessed. Sore, cracked or crusted nipples: finding the cause Nipple damage may come from feeding, pumping, friction or a skin condition. Early help can reduce pain and identify changes that need examination. Bumps on the nipple or areola: what they might be Normal glands, irritated skin, milk blebs and infections can look different but overlap. Learn what to leave alone and when to get a lump checked. Tingling or burning breasts during feeding: what to notice Understand let-down, latch pain, inflammation, vasospasm and other breast changes, with practical comfort measures and signs that need assessment. Transient tachypnoea: when a newborn breathes too fast Why retained lung fluid can cause fast breathing after birth, how the neonatal team checks it, and what recovery may involve. Cross-cradle and other breastfeeding positions: finding your fit Try cradle, underarm, side-lying and cross-cradle holds with clear hand placement, comfortable support and safer feeding habits. Feeding support for babies with a cleft or low muscle tone Understand cleft feeding, the Dancer hand hold, Down syndrome, milk transfer and when a baby needs specialist help. When your baby refuses the breast Why a baby may pull away or refuse breastfeeding, from early attachment difficulties to distraction and nursing strikes, and how to protect their intake while getting help. Ibuprofen while breastfeeding: doses, precautions and pain relief Learn how ibuprofen fits with breastfeeding, why product-specific dosing matters, and how aspirin, naproxen, codeine and infant treatment differ. Vitamin K deficiency bleeding: why the newborn injection matters Babies begin life with low vitamin K stores. The injection after birth helps prevent serious bleeding, which may occur without an early warning. Can you take ondansetron while breastfeeding? Ondansetron, also known as Zofran, can be used during breastfeeding when appropriate. Current human data are reassuring, but the cause of nausea still matters. Is your breastfed baby constipated? Hard, painful stools matter more than a missed day. Learn how age changes what is normal, when feeding needs checking and which remedies need advice. How to breastfeed while lying on your side A practical guide to side-lying feeds, comfortable attachment and returning your baby to a separate sleep space. Helping your baby move between breast and bottle Some babies need time and support to switch feeding methods. Protect milk intake, watch feeding cues and avoid blaming every difficulty on nipple confusion. Foods and drinks while breastfeeding: what needs attention? Practical guidance on fish, caffeine, alcohol, herbal products and suspected food allergy, with a varied diet instead of unnecessary restrictions. Breastfeeding with psoriasis: care for your skin and your baby Psoriasis is not contagious, and breastfeeding is often possible. A medication-specific plan can treat symptoms while limiting your baby’s exposure. Cow’s milk protein allergy: recognising it and planning feeds Milk allergy can cause immediate or delayed symptoms. Diagnosis and a suitable feeding plan help avoid both unsafe exposure and unnecessary restrictions. When your milk volume is slow to increase after birth Understand delayed milk production, get feeding assessed and build a plan that supports your supply while keeping your newborn well fed. Neonatal lupus: antibodies, newborn symptoms and specialist care Understand how neonatal lupus differs from adult lupus, which changes may resolve, why heart block needs separate care and how pregnancy monitoring is individualized. Why breast milk can look different colours Understand normal milk shades, changes with feeding and storage, and when pink, red, brown or black milk needs advice. Breast-milk jaundice: feeding, checks and follow-up Breast-milk jaundice can persist in a well-growing baby, but poor feeding, unusual sleepiness and prolonged yellowing need proper assessment. Can you increase your milk supply in one day? What can help today, how to check whether supply is low, and the limits of power pumping, lactation foods and quick-fix advice. White spots on the nipple: milk blebs and other causes Understand milk blebs, normal areolar glands, infection and persistent nipple changes, with practical guidance on feeding and when to seek care. Can you switch or combine infant formula brands? Changing formula can be possible, but each product needs the right preparation and some babies need a specialist plan. Cleaning your baby’s mouth and tongue: a gentle start to oral care How to care for a baby’s gums, recognise milk coating and possible thrush, and begin brushing when the first tooth appears. Encephalocele: diagnosis, treatment and support for your child What an encephalocele is, how specialists assess it before or after birth, and why surgery and ongoing support are tailored to each child. Postpartum recovery: what to avoid and when to ask for help A practical guide to rest, bleeding, pain, mood, contraception, food and support after birth, including symptoms that need urgent attention. Gripe water for babies: safety, evidence and other ways to soothe What is in gripe water, does it help colic, and is it safe for a newborn? Explore ingredient concerns, feeding support and signs that need medical help. Newborn sneezing: what is normal and when to get help Frequent sneezing can be normal in newborns. Learn what the reflex does, which symptoms matter, and why sneezing alone cannot diagnose illness or withdrawal. Snoring and noisy breathing in babies: causes and when to seek help Understand nasal snuffles, snoring and stridor in babies, how laryngomalacia is assessed, and which feeding or breathing changes need urgent care. Why does my newborn stay awake at night? Five reasons to consider Explore newborn night waking, feeding, day–night cues, discomfort and stimulation, with realistic expectations and safe ways to support sleep. Why is my newborn’s skin peeling? Understand normal newborn peeling, vernix and birth timing, how eczema differs, and gentle skin care with clear signs for medical review. Apert syndrome: signs, diagnosis and care Learn how Apert syndrome affects the skull, face, hands and feet, what FGFR2 inheritance means, and how a specialist team plans treatment and support. Stickler syndrome: causes, signs and ongoing care Understand the variable signs of Stickler syndrome, collagen-related inheritance, retinal warning signs and coordinated care for hearing, joints, feeding and growth. Torticollis: a tilted neck in babies, children and adults Understand infant muscular torticollis, other causes of a head tilt, warning signs and how physiotherapy and specialist treatment differ by diagnosis. Burping a sleepy baby: gentle holds and safe sleep A baby need not burp after every feed. Learn gentle supported holds, when to stop trying, responsive feeding, reflux precautions and signs needing medical help. Herbal lactation drops: ingredients, evidence and feeding safety What nine common galactagogue ingredients can and cannot do, how to assess milk supply, and when a feeding problem needs prompt care. Kernicterus: severe newborn jaundice and urgent warning signs How severe bilirubin buildup can injure a newborn’s brain, the warning signs needing emergency care, and how testing, treatment and follow-up reduce risk. Breastfeeding with COVID-19: feeding, precautions and support Breastfeeding can usually continue with COVID-19. Understand close-contact precautions, expressed milk, safe equipment cleaning, medicines and infant warning signs. Robin sequence: breathing, feeding and growing with specialist care How a small lower jaw and backward tongue position can affect a newborn’s airway, feeding and palate, and why assessment and follow-up must be individual. Flat head syndrome in babies: plagiocephaly and safe sleep Learn how positional head flattening differs from craniosynostosis, when to seek assessment, and how supervised tummy time, physiotherapy or selected helmets may help. Antibiotics while breastfeeding: medicine safety and infant monitoring Learn how breastfeeding antibiotic choices are assessed, what infant symptoms need advice, and when a temporary feeding plan may be necessary. Oesophageal atresia and tracheoesophageal fistula: newborn care and follow-up Understand the five anatomical patterns, newborn warning signs, specialist diagnosis, surgery, long-gap care and ongoing feeding and breathing support. Asafoetida while breastfeeding: spice, remedies and safety Understand hing, unproven milk-supply claims, limited lactation evidence and the important difference between seasoning food and giving a remedy to a baby. Aloe vera while breastfeeding: gel, oral products and safety Separate skin gel from aloe latex and drinks, understand limited milk-transfer data, and review nipple care, skin and hair claims, side effects and safer next steps. Passionflower while breastfeeding: benefits, uncertainty and safer support What passionflower research can and cannot tell us about breastfeeding, sleep and postpartum mood, with practical medicine checks and urgent warning signs. Konar or sidr while breastfeeding: identity, claims and uncertain safety Konar and sidr names can refer to different plants. Understand the limits of breastfeeding evidence, milk-detox claims and advice after fruit or herbal-product use. Medlar while breastfeeding: food safety and unproven benefits Common medlar can be a food choice, but it has no established special breastfeeding benefit. Learn about bletting, seeds, supplements and symptoms needing care. Plantago herbs while breastfeeding: plant identity, evidence and safer choices Plantago leaf remedies are not the same as psyllium husk. Understand uncertain breastfeeding safety, traditional claims, product-specific risks and when to seek care. Cumin while breastfeeding: food, supplements and milk-supply claims What cumin research can and cannot show about milk supply, infant colic, postpartum hair loss and the safety of concentrated herbal products. Postpartum thyroiditis: changing symptoms, recovery and follow-up Thyroid inflammation after birth can cause a high-hormone phase, a low-hormone phase or both. Learn the symptoms, risk factors and follow-up to discuss. Anophthalmia and microphthalmia: early eye and vision care Understand absent or small eyes from birth, possible causes, prenatal and newborn assessment, visual potential, conformers and coordinated family support. Lumbar puncture in a newborn: tests, comfort and aftercare Why a newborn may need a cerebrospinal-fluid sample, what the team checks, how comfort and safety are managed, and what happens after the procedure. Kidney dysplasia in babies: development, function and care Understand abnormal kidney development, why function varies in one- and two-sided dysplasia, and how scans, follow-up and treatment are individualized. CHARGE syndrome: diagnosis, health care and communication support Understand the variable CHARGE pattern, CHD7 testing, breathing and feeding priorities, sensory and hormone care, and practical long-term support for children and families. Hormones after birth: changes, recovery and when to seek help How estrogen, progesterone, prolactin and oxytocin change after birth, why recovery varies, and when symptoms need medical assessment. Micrognathia: assessing a small lower jaw How a small lower jaw is assessed before and after birth, its possible associations, breathing and feeding concerns, and individual observation or treatment. Hepatitis C and breastfeeding: milk, blood exposure and follow-up Breastfeeding with hepatitis C, what to do about cracked or bleeding nipples, blood precautions, parent and infant testing, and treatment decisions. Bowel changes after birth: what to expect and when to get help The first bowel movement, constipation, diarrhea and anal discomfort after vaginal or cesarean birth: practical care and warning signs. Gas and bloating after birth: causes, comfort and when to get help Understand postpartum gas, food and swallowed air, constipation and wind-control problems, with safer care and warning signs after either type of birth. Is my newborn’s heart healthy? Checks, symptoms and when to get help Understand newborn heart checks, what a reassuring screen cannot exclude, and why murmurs, feeding changes, breathing trouble or repeated choking need assessment. Baby fontanelles: soft-spot care, closure and warning signs Learn what baby soft spots do, how to handle the head gently, why closure varies, and when a sunken or bulging fontanelle needs urgent care. Smith–Lemli–Opitz syndrome: diagnosis, inheritance and care Understand SLOS, DHCR7 and sterol testing, variable features, family recurrence, individual care and the limits of cholesterol and simvastatin treatment evidence. Congenital diaphragmatic hernia: lungs, treatment and follow-up Understand CDH types, underdeveloped lungs, newborn symptoms, specialist treatment and long-term breathing, feeding and developmental care. Sticky eyes in newborns: discharge, blocked tear ducts and treatment Understand newborn yellow eye discharge, safe cleaning, clinician-taught massage, infection warning signs and when tear-duct procedures may help. Omphalocele: diagnosis, associated conditions and treatment Understand a sac-covered abdominal-wall defect, prenatal tests, uncertain causes and specialist newborn care with primary, staged or delayed repair. Breastfeeding with small breasts: size, milk and support Small breasts do not by themselves mean low milk supply. Understand storage, breast changes, surgery, comfortable feeding and signs your baby needs help. Exclusive expressing: feeding your baby expressed breast milk Plan exclusive expressing from the early days: comfortable pumping, milk amounts, bottle feeds, safe handling, work, contraception and a sustainable routine. Diastasis recti: recognising abdominal separation and planning recovery Understand abdominal muscle separation during and after pregnancy, the limits of a home check, rehabilitation and when further assessment or surgery may be considered. Dehydration in babies: signs, feeding and getting help Recognise dehydration from low milk intake, illness or heat, and understand urgent assessment, feeding support and supervised rehydration for babies. Grapefruit while breastfeeding: food benefits and medicine checks Grapefruit can fit a varied breastfeeding diet, but whole fruit and juice interact with some medicines. Understand nutrition, infant symptoms and extracts. Argan oil while breastfeeding: skin, hair, food and infant contact What argan oil can and cannot do for skin and hair, how food and cosmetic products differ, and why nipple use and direct infant contact need separate advice.

title: Baby & Child
description: Milestones, feeding, sleep, and positive parenting as your baby grows into a curious, confident child.
body: Baby Milestones Month by Month (0–12 Months) A friendly guide to baby milestones in the first year: motor, social, and language skills by quarter, why every baby has their own pace, and when to check in with a doctor. Starting Solids: Baby’s First Foods How to know your baby is ready for solids around 6 months, great first foods, purees vs baby-led weaning, introducing allergens, and what to avoid. Baby Sleep Training: Gentle Approaches That Work An honest look at gentle sleep training: when babies are ready, how fading, pick-up-put-down, and graduated check-ins work, and why consistency beats any single method. Teething: Signs, Timeline, and Soothing Tips When baby teeth typically arrive, which teething symptoms are real vs myth, safe ways to soothe sore gums, what to avoid, and dental care from the first tooth. Childhood Vaccinations: A Simple Overview How childhood vaccines work in plain language, why schedules are timed the way they are, common mild reactions and comfort tips, and how to keep good records. Toddler Nutrition and Feeding Picky Eaters Realistic toddler portions, the division of responsibility, proven picky-eating strategies, milk and juice guidance, and how to end food battles for good. Speech and Language Development in Toddlers How language unfolds from babble to sentences, everyday ways to encourage talking, why bilingual homes are an advantage, and red flags worth discussing with a provider. Positive Parenting and Gentle Discipline How gentle discipline actually works: connection before correction, realistic expectations, redirection, natural consequences, naming feelings, and repairing after hard moments. Potty Training: When and How to Start How to spot true potty-training readiness, prepare gear and expectations, follow a calm step-by-step approach, handle accidents without shame, and ride out regressions. Screen Time and Healthy Habits for Young Children Realistic screen time guidance for babies and toddlers: general limits by age, quality over quantity, co-viewing, screen-free zones, and modeling habits without guilt. 2 Month Old Milestones: What Babies Do by 2 Months A clear guide to 2 month old milestones: social smiles, cooing, head control, feeding and sleep patterns, what the checkup covers, and the signs that deserve a call to your baby's clinician. 4 Month Old Milestones: Skills to Expect at 4 Months A calm guide to 4 month old milestones: the social, language, movement, and feeding skills most babies show by four months, plus sleep basics and signs worth a pediatrician visit. 6 Month Old Milestones: What Babies Do by 6 Months A calm guide to 6 month old milestones: the social, language, movement, feeding, and sleep skills most babies show by half a year, plus signs worth mentioning to your pediatrician. 9 Month Old Milestones: Skills to Expect at 9 Months A calm guide to 9 month old milestones: the social, language, thinking, and movement skills most babies show, what the 9 month checkup covers, and when to call your pediatrician. 12 Month Old Milestones: Your Baby at 1 Year A calm guide to 12 month old milestones: the social, language, cognitive, and movement skills most babies show at 1 year, plus what the 12 month checkup covers. Sleep Regression Ages: 4, 8, 12 and 18 Month Guide A calm guide to sleep regression ages: what happens at 4, 8, 12, and 18 months and 2 years, how long each lasts, and how to respond. Nap Transition Ages: 3 to 2, 2 to 1, and Dropping Naps A practical guide to nap transition ages: when babies drop from three naps to two, two to one, and no nap at all, plus readiness signs and schedule tips. Introducing Allergens to Baby: Peanut, Egg and More A calm, practical guide to introducing allergens to baby: when to start peanut and egg, safe first forms, how often to repeat, and which reactions need a call or urgent care. Baby Finger Foods: What to Offer by Age and Choking Safety A practical guide to baby finger foods: when to start, how to cut each food safely by age, which choking hazards to avoid, and how to tell gagging from choking. When Can Babies Drink Water? Cup Training by Age When can babies drink water? Not before 6 months, then small sips with meals. A plain guide to water amounts by age, open and straw cups, and the bottle wean. How to Soothe a Teething Baby: Safe Remedies That Work A calm, practical guide to how to soothe a teething baby: chilled teethers, gum massage, honest medicine rules, and the popular remedies that safety experts say to skip. Babyproofing Checklist: How to Childproof Room by Room A practical babyproofing checklist you can finish in a weekend: anchoring furniture, placing stair gates, covering outlets, and locking away medicines, cleaners, and button batteries before your baby starts to crawl. Car Seat Guidelines by Age: Rear Facing to Booster Clear car seat guidelines by age: how long to stay rear facing, when to move to a forward-facing harness, when a booster is enough, and when the front seat becomes safe. Language Activities for Toddlers: Games by Age Simple language activities for toddlers and babies, organized by age: serve and return games, copycat sounds, naming walks, and talking games you can play in the next ten minutes with zero prep. Separation Anxiety in Babies and Toddlers: What Helps What separation anxiety in babies and toddlers looks like, when it starts and fades, and calm, practical ways to make goodbyes, drop-offs, and nights easier. Baby and Toddler Tantrums: How to Respond Learn why baby and toddler tantrums happen from ages 1 to 3, how to respond calmly during a meltdown, and when to talk with a pediatrician. Starting Daycare: How to Ease the Transition for Your Child A calm, week-by-week plan for starting daycare: how to prepare your child, handle drop-off tears, know what to pack, and spot signs that deserve a conversation with your provider. Potty Training Readiness: Signs Your Toddler Is Ready How to tell if your toddler is ready to potty train: a calm potty training readiness checklist of physical, language, and emotional signs, plus the times when waiting works better. Early-Morning Waking: A Gentle Troubleshooting Guide Why toddlers and preschoolers may wake too early, how to check sleep timing, light, hunger, and routines, and when to ask about a health concern. Balanced Meals for Toddlers: Structure Without Pressure How to offer balanced toddler meals, handle picky phases, share responsibility for eating, and keep choking safety and growth in view. Building a Family Allergy Action Plan How to prepare for a child’s food or environmental allergy, share clear instructions with caregivers, and recognize symptoms that need urgent help. Welcoming a New Sibling With Less Pressure How to prepare an older child for a new baby, protect their connection with caregivers, respond to big feelings, and make the first weeks more manageable. Independent Play: Helping Toddlers Build Attention and Confidence How to create a safe play invitation, start with short stretches, stay available without taking over, and understand why independent play develops gradually. Toddler Biting: Calm Limits and Practical Prevention Why toddlers bite, what to do in the moment, how to protect other children, and how to teach safer ways to communicate without shame. Building a Family Reading Routine That Actually Lasts How shared reading supports language and connection, how to choose books, keep a routine flexible, and include children who do not sit still for a whole story. When Do Babies Roll Over? Timeline and Safety Guide When do babies roll over? Usually tummy to back around 4 months and back to tummy around 5 to 6 months, plus the swaddle and sleep changes rolling triggers. When Do Babies Sit Up? Timeline, Help, and Safety When do babies sit up? Most sit with support around 4 to 6 months and without support by 6 to 9 months. Here is how to help, safely. When Do Babies Crawl? Ages, Styles, and What Is Normal When do babies crawl? Often between 7 and 10 months, though the range is wide and some babies skip crawling entirely. Here is what to watch and when to check in. When Do Babies Start Walking? Timeline and What Helps Wondering when babies start walking? Most take first steps around 12 months, with a normal range of about 9 to 18 months, following a sequence of pulling up, cruising, and standing alone. When Do Babies Sleep Through the Night? When do babies sleep through the night? Often between 4 and 6 months for a 5 to 6 hour stretch, though night waking stays normal well into the first year. 4 Month Old Sleep Schedule: A Flexible Day Build a flexible four-month sleep routine with an example timeline, clear sleep-log totals, missing-data guidance and safe-sleep sources. 6 Month Old Feeding Schedule: Milk and First Foods Plan a flexible six-month feeding routine around milk, readiness and feeding cues, with a practical day guide and printable observation sheet. Helping your child leave the pacifier behind Plan the timing, build other ways to settle and choose a gradual reduction or goodbye day with safe, responsive support. Vomiting without a fever in babies and children: causes and when to get help Distinguish spit-up from vomiting, understand ten possible causes without fever, and recognise dehydration or symptoms needing urgent assessment. Why a child may vomit at night: causes, care and warning signs What nighttime vomiting may mean, how food reactions, cough, reflux and breathing problems differ, and when your child needs urgent help. Blood in a toddler’s stool: causes, care and when to get help Understand possible causes of red or black stool, which symptoms need urgent care, and how children are assessed and treated. Tongue thrust in children: when to ask for an assessment Recognise persistent tongue-thrust patterns, understand their possible causes and learn how dental, medical and speech professionals assess them. Psoriasis in babies and children: signs, types and care Learn how childhood psoriasis can look, how it differs from common rashes, and which skin changes need routine or urgent assessment. HPV vaccination for children: timing, protection and safety Why HPV vaccination is offered before exposure, how US and Canadian dose schedules differ, and what parents can ask about protection and side effects. Breast development: soreness, uneven growth and changes to check Learn how breasts change from puberty onward, why tenderness and asymmetry happen, and which lumps, skin changes or discharge need medical advice. Flu vaccines for children: timing, doses and safety How to plan a child’s flu vaccine, understand age and dose rules, discuss allergies and recognize reactions that need medical help. Breastfeeding beyond the first year What continued breastfeeding can offer, how milk changes, and practical ways to manage toddler meals, boundaries, night feeds and gradual weaning. IQ and emotional intelligence: different skills, not competing labels Understand cognitive and emotional assessments, what scores can predict, and the evidence behind learning, reading and training claims. A child’s broken or knocked-out tooth: what to do next Check the child first, contact a dentist promptly and handle lost teeth carefully. Baby and permanent teeth need different first aid. A blue bump on the gum: understanding eruption cysts An eruption cyst can appear before a baby or adult tooth comes through. Most settle naturally, but persistent, painful or infected swellings need a dentist. Prune juice for a constipated child: age matters Understand when prune juice may help, why newborns need a different approach and how to support comfortable stools safely. When do babies learn to stand? Standing develops through several skills. Support your baby with safe play, understand milestone checks and know when to ask for an assessment. When your toddler refuses food: gentle ideas and when to get help Understand changing toddler appetites, make meals less pressured and recognise signs that food refusal needs a feeding or medical assessment. Why toddlers hit or bang their head, and how to respond Understand possible reasons for head-hitting, respond calmly and safely, and recognize when injury, pain or developmental concerns need assessment. Why your child’s teeth may look yellow Understand normal tooth colour, staining, injury and enamel changes, with safe daily care and a guide to treatments a paediatric dentist may consider. When your toddler holds in poo: breaking the constipation cycle Understand stool withholding, support comfortable toileting and learn why early constipation treatment matters more than pressure or bigger rewards. Tooth decay in children: causes, treatment and prevention Why baby teeth matter, how to recognise possible decay, what dental treatments involve and how brushing, fluoride and food routines can help protect teeth. Viral gastroenteritis in children: fluids, feeding and warning signs Care for vomiting and diarrhoea with appropriate fluids and food, recognise dehydration, and know when a child needs urgent help. When do baby teeth fall out? A complete guide to baby-tooth eruption and loss, adult molars and premolars, loose-tooth care, timing differences and when to see the dentist. MiraLAX for children: understanding the treatment plan Understand PEG 3350, child-specific prescribing, treatment stages, side effects, reported behaviour changes and the food and toilet routines that support recovery. When your child cannot pass a hard stool Recognise constipation and impaction, respond to a painful stool safely, and understand assessment, treatment and prevention. Toddler’s diarrhoea: food and drink changes that may help Persistent loose stools in a growing, otherwise well toddler can have a functional cause. Learn about balanced meals, juice, fibre and signs needing reassessment. Seven simple ways to play and learn together Everyday conversation, movement, music and safe games give babies and toddlers chances to explore without expensive classes or special equipment. Branchial cleft cysts and small openings in the neck A branchial cleft remnant can cause a neck lump or repeated drainage. Assessment identifies the structure and guides treatment. COVID vaccination and future fertility: questions for teenagers and families What fertility research shows, how mRNA works, why menstrual changes are different from infertility, and what to ask about current vaccine advice and real side effects. COVID-19 vaccine side effects in children: what parents should know Common reactions, rare heart and allergic complications, comfort measures and current questions to discuss before a child’s COVID-19 vaccination. Does masturbation cause acne? What actually helps breakouts Separate the puberty myth from the causes of acne, then build a gentle skin routine and know when professional treatment is worth seeking. Surgery for an undescended testicle: a guide for parents Why early assessment matters, how orchidopexy is planned and what to ask about your child’s recovery and follow-up. Genital growth during puberty: size, timing and when to seek advice Understand how genital development progresses, why age charts and comparisons can mislead, and how to respond to a young person’s concerns with privacy and appropriate care. Early puberty: when to seek advice and what assessment involves Understand early body changes, the reasons for assessment and how monitoring or treatment can support an individual child. Can growth hormone injections make you taller after puberty? Understand remaining growth, genuine hormone deficiency, childhood treatment and why adult replacement does not lengthen bones after growth plates close. Can you grow taller after puberty? What healthy habits can and cannot do Understand growth plates, puberty timing and six practical approaches to nutrition, sleep, exercise, supplements, posture and growth concerns. Can exercise make you taller? Ten movements and what they really do Understand height, growth plates and posture, then explore ten familiar exercises as options for comfortable movement and fitness. Eight ways to enjoy free time with your teenager Plan cooking, outings, hobbies, movement and games with your teenager while making room for friends, rest and growing independence. Growth and puberty in girls: what the timing can tell you How height growth changes before and after the first period, which factors influence puberty, and when a growth pattern deserves assessment. Growth and puberty in boys: what changes and when to ask for help Understand the usual sequence of puberty, why growth rates differ and when early or delayed changes need assessment. Talking with your daughter about puberty How to start calm, practical conversations about puberty, prepare for a first period and support a child whose development feels earlier or later than her friends’. What teenagers need from their parents Eight practical ways to support affection, independence, belonging, identity, privacy, exploration, skills and enjoyment while keeping clear boundaries. Dextrocardia: understanding a right-sided heart Learn what dextrocardia means, why associated heart and organ conditions matter, and how assessment, treatment and follow-up differ between children. Partridge meat for children: nutrition and safe preparation Partridge can be a food choice, but its source, cooking and texture matter. Learn about lead-shot game, allergy, starting solids and exaggerated health claims. Dandy–Walker malformation: signs, diagnosis and care Understand Dandy–Walker malformation, how it differs from other scan findings, and the role of imaging, genetic counselling and support. Ostrich meat for children: nutrition, textures and safe preparation Ostrich meat can be one protein option. Learn when to introduce it, how to adapt the texture, what nutrition claims mean and how to reduce choking and food-safety risks. Swollen lymph nodes in children: what to notice and when to get help Why children develop swollen glands, how skin infections and eczema can contribute, and which changes need prompt medical assessment. Newborn cone-shaped head: normal moulding and when to seek care A newborn’s head may look pointed after birth. Learn how moulding changes, how to protect safe sleep, and which swelling or persistent head-shape changes need assessment. Poland syndrome: variable features, diagnosis and individual care Understand the chest-muscle difference in Poland syndrome, possible hand, rib and breast features, uncertain causes and personalized support and treatment. Moebius syndrome: signs, diagnosis and lifelong support Understand Moebius syndrome, its variable facial, eye and feeding effects, uncertain causes and inheritance, and practical specialist support. Heterotaxy: organ differences, assessment and lifelong care Heterotaxy can affect the heart, lungs, spleen and digestive organs. Learn about individual assessment, treatment and urgent warning signs. Hydranencephaly: signs, diagnosis and supportive care Understand hydranencephaly, specialist diagnosis, feeding and seizure care, shunt limits, urgent symptoms and support for families. Phimosis: tight foreskin, care and warning signs A foreskin that does not pull back can be normal in childhood. Learn about symptoms, scarring, clinician-led treatments and the emergency signs of paraphimosis. Caput succedaneum: newborn scalp swelling and when to seek help Understand birth-related caput swelling, how it differs from other scalp swellings, expected improvement, jaundice checks and urgent warning signs. When babies recognize their name: signs and when to seek help Learn how babies respond to their name, gentle ways to support communication, how recognition differs from speaking, and when hearing or developmental checks can help. Laryngomalacia in babies: noisy breathing, feeding and treatment Learn what laryngomalacia means, how doctors assess noisy breathing, feeding and growth, when surgery helps and which signs need emergency care. Lissencephaly: diagnosis, development and care What reduced brain folding means, why prenatal scans have limits, and how children with lissencephaly receive individual support for seizures, feeding and development. Anorectal malformations: an absent or misplaced anus in a newborn Understand newborn anorectal malformations, urgent signs, associated conditions, genetic counselling, surgery and longer-term bowel and urinary care. Megalencephaly in children: brain growth, assessment and care Learn how enlarged brain tissue differs from a large head, possible causes and symptoms, how children are assessed, and why treatment and outlook are individual. Osgood–Schlatter knee pain: activity, treatment and recovery Learn why Osgood–Schlatter causes pain below the kneecap, how activity can be adapted, which comfort measures help and when knee pain needs urgent assessment. Sever’s disease: heel pain in growing children Understand growth-related heel pain, warning signs, diagnosis and a practical plan for activity, footwear, pain relief and returning to sport. Klippel–Feil syndrome: fused neck vertebrae, diagnosis and care Understand congenital neck-vertebra fusion, variable signs and genetic causes, associated conditions, selected tests, safe activity, treatment and follow-up into adulthood. Mosaic Down syndrome: features, testing and individual support Understand mosaic Down syndrome, why sample percentages cannot predict ability, how screening differs from diagnosis and which health and developmental supports matter. Pallister–Killian syndrome: mosaicism, diagnosis and lifelong care Understand Pallister–Killian syndrome, its variable features, why blood testing can miss it, prenatal testing limits and individualized developmental and medical support. Pulmonary valve stenosis in babies and children: can it be treated? Understand a narrowed pulmonary heart valve, its symptoms and tests, when monitoring or a procedure may help, and which signs in a baby need emergency care. Aortic valve stenosis in children: severity, treatment and follow-up Understand mild, moderate, severe and critical aortic valve stenosis, how an echocardiogram assesses it, when babies need emergency care and why follow-up continues after treatment. Ring chromosome 14 syndrome: genetics, seizures and care Understand ring chromosome 14 syndrome, chromosome testing, variable development, epilepsy care and emergency warning signs for families. Orbital hypertelorism: what wider eye spacing can mean Learn how orbital hypertelorism differs from telecanthus, how clinicians assess associated conditions, and why scans, surgery and timing are individual. Cryptophthalmos: types, vision and specialist treatment Learn how complete, incomplete and abortive cryptophthalmos differ, why assessment includes Fraser syndrome, and how specialists protect vision and plan individualized care. Coarctation of the aorta: symptoms, treatment and lifelong care Understand narrowing of the main artery, newborn warning signs, associated heart conditions, treatment options and why follow-up continues after repair. Atrioventricular septal defect: symptoms, repair and lifelong care Understand complete and partial AVSD, infant warning signs, diagnosis, surgery, follow-up and individualized pregnancy planning. Hypoplastic left heart syndrome: symptoms, circulation and care Understand HLHS symptoms, why newborn circulation can deteriorate quickly, and how specialist treatment, feeding support and lifelong follow-up help. Kyphosis in children: rounded backs, causes and care Understand flexible posture and structural kyphosis, childhood symptoms, assessment, monitoring, braces and surgery, plus urgent warning signs. Dysphagia in children: swallowing signs, assessment and support Learn the signs of swallowing difficulties in babies and children, including silent aspiration, and how a pediatric team plans safe feeding and treatment. Dates while breastfeeding: nutrition, safety and milk supply Dates can fit a varied breastfeeding diet. Learn what a small milk-supply trial found, what remains uncertain and when feeding concerns need help. Jacobsen syndrome: understanding 11q deletion and care Jacobsen syndrome affects people differently. Learn about genetic diagnosis, bleeding and heart risks, development and an individual care plan. Tetralogy of Fallot: diagnosis, treatment and lifelong care Understand the four heart changes in tetralogy of Fallot, variable symptoms, blue-spell emergencies, surgery and follow-up through adulthood. Childhood tics and Tourette syndrome: choosing support and treatment Understand tic assessment, when treatment can help, CBIT, school and family support, coexisting ADHD or OCD, and safe medicine follow-up. Multicystic dysplastic kidney in babies: diagnosis and follow-up What MCDK means, how scans assess both kidneys, and why treatment and follow-up depend on the remaining kidney and the baby's overall health. Hepatoblastoma in children: symptoms, treatment and follow-up Understand this childhood liver cancer, the role of AFP and scans, surgery and chemotherapy, selected other treatments, and support during follow-up. Hemihyperplasia and lateralized overgrowth: assessment and follow-up Understand one-sided body growth, genetic assessment, individual tumour-surveillance plans, limb-length care and changes that need medical attention. Cyclopia: prenatal diagnosis, prognosis and family care Understand cyclopia and severe holoprosencephaly, specialist scans and genetic testing, the very poor prognosis, recurrence questions and support for families. Children with one functioning kidney: care, sport and growing up Understand a missing or nonfunctioning kidney, selective testing, lifelong checks and individual sports decisions for children with one functioning kidney. Heart failure in babies and children: symptoms, causes and care Understand pediatric heart failure, feeding and breathing signs, different causes, specialist treatment and nutrition, and which changes need emergency help. Skeletal dysplasias: signs, diagnosis and lifelong care Understand the varied bone and cartilage conditions called skeletal dysplasias, how they are assessed, and how treatment supports health and daily life. Dry eyes in children: symptoms, eye tests and care Understand possible childhood dry-eye symptoms, how an eye examination helps, and care for screen strain, eyelid problems, lenses and other causes. When your child does not join other children’s play Understand why a child watches, wanders or avoids peer play, how to offer gentle support at home and preschool, and when to ask for assessment. Mosquito bites in babies and children: relief and prevention How to care for a suspected mosquito bite, choose age-appropriate itch relief, recognize warning signs and reduce further bites safely. Sunburn in babies and children: care, warning signs and prevention Recognise sunburn, know when a baby needs medical advice, soothe injured skin safely and plan shade, clothing and sunscreen for the next outing. Can you tell whether a baby is intelligent? Seven common claims examined What early milestones, attention, curiosity, birth weight and alertness can (and cannot) tell you about a baby’s development, with safe ways to support learning. When a child has big emotional reactions: noticing patterns, responding and finding support Understand intense outbursts or withdrawal, observe feelings without a sensitivity score, use ten practical caregiving approaches and know when assessment or support may help. Supporting children online: privacy, messages and what to do when something goes wrong Stay involved in children’s online communication, agree privacy and safety boundaries, respond calmly to harmful messages and use reporting routes without spreading intimate images. Microtia and ear-canal atresia: hearing, care and reconstruction A family guide to microtia and ear-canal atresia: early hearing assessment, hearing devices, communication support, reconstruction choices and coordinated care. 3 Month Old Sleep: A Flexible Daily Rhythm Explore a flexible sleep rhythm for a 3 month old, understand wake windows, record naps and night waking, and find age-specific sleep guides. 7–8 Month Old Feeding: Milk, Meals and Texture Plan a flexible feeding rhythm at 7–8 months, balance milk and complementary foods, compare textures and record useful observations with BeMama.

title: About BeMama
description: How BeMama supports every stage (Daily Journey, Q&A, community, and tools) and how to get started.
body: BeMama: Pregnancy Guidance and Baby Tracking Meet BeMama: pregnancy guidance, a baby tracker for feeding and sleep, and free website tools for planning and everyday care. Pregnancy Tracker App: BeMama Daily Journey Use BeMama’s pregnancy tracker app to follow your week, set up Daily Journey and understand pregnancy date estimates and feature access. Q&A and Community: Ask, Learn, and Connect How BeMama’s Q&A and community spaces work: ask questions, browse related discussions, and find supportive, moderated connection with others on the same journey. title: Preconception Health: How to Prepare Your Body for Pregnancy
description: A practical preconception checklist (nutrition, prenatal vitamins, health checks, lifestyle changes, and when to start) to give your future pregnancy the healthiest possible start.
body: The months before you start trying can matter just as much as pregnancy itself. Preparing your body early gives a baby the healthiest possible foundation and can make conceiving smoother. Here is a clear, practical checklist to work through. Start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid Begin taking a daily prenatal vitamin containing folic acid ideally two to three months before you try to conceive. Adequate folic acid in the earliest weeks (often before you know you are pregnant) significantly lowers the risk of neural tube defects. Look for a prenatal that also includes iron, iodine, and vitamin D, and confirm the right dose with your healthcare provider, since some people need more. Book a preconception check-up A visit with your doctor before pregnancy is one of the most valuable steps. It is a chance to review your medical history, current medications, family history, vaccinations, and any chronic conditions such as diabetes, thyroid issues, or high blood pressure that are best stabilized beforehand. Ask which of your medications and supplements are safe to continue, and whether any screening or vaccines (like rubella) should be updated first. Nourish your body Aim for a balanced, whole-food diet: plenty of vegetables and fruit, whole grains, lean protein, healthy fats, and calcium and iron-rich foods. There is no single "fertility diet," but overall nutrition supports hormonal balance and a healthy weight. Reaching a healthy weight range before pregnancy can improve fertility and reduce risks, so small, sustainable changes now are worthwhile. Adjust lifestyle habits Stop smoking and avoid alcohol and recreational drugs, which affect both fertility and early development. Keep caffeine moderate. Prioritize sleep, gentle regular exercise, and stress management. Chronic stress and exhaustion can affect cycles, and building good routines now makes the transition into pregnancy easier. Prepare your mind and your calendar Learning how your menstrual cycle works helps you identify your fertile window once you begin trying. It also helps to talk openly with your partner about timing, expectations, and support. Give yourself grace: for most healthy couples conception can take several months, and that is completely normal. Start a folic-acid prenatal vitamin 2–3 months before trying. Book a preconception check-up to review medications, conditions, and vaccines. Eat a balanced diet and aim for a healthy weight range. Stop smoking, avoid alcohol, and moderate caffeine. Learn your cycle and be patient: conception often takes a few months. How far in advance should I start preparing? Aim to begin about three months ahead, mainly so folic acid levels build up before the earliest weeks of pregnancy. Even a few weeks of preparation is better than none. Does my partner need to prepare too? Yes. Sperm take roughly three months to develop, so a partner improving diet, limiting alcohol, and avoiding smoking during that window supports healthier sperm. Do I need to stop birth control early? Fertility usually returns quickly after stopping most methods, though cycles can take a little time to settle. Your provider can advise based on the method you use.

title: Understanding Your Menstrual Cycle and Fertile Window
description: Learn how the menstrual cycle works, when ovulation happens, and how to identify your fertile window so you can time intercourse for the best chance of conceiving.
body: Knowing how your cycle works is the single most useful skill when you are trying to conceive. It tells you when you are most likely to get pregnant (your fertile window) so you can focus your efforts on the right days. The phases of the menstrual cycle A cycle is counted from the first day of one period to the first day of the next. It has two main phases: the follicular phase (from your period until ovulation) and the luteal phase (from ovulation until your next period). The average cycle is about 28 days, but anywhere from roughly 21 to 35 days is common.
